note: Adapted from Sjöstedt's (1900) original description of Termes nobilis, written in German; the alate is recorded as unknown in the original; most figures in the two measurement columns could not be recovered owing to OCR damage and are omitted, so several characters are compared with the corresponding measurements of T. lilljeborgi; specimen records are not translated.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: head shining above, dark brownish black or black, paler below, reddish brown, postmentum dark with a similar, more or less distinct band on each side; head rectangular, narrowed anteriorly, posterior angles rounded, upper surface flatly convex on each side; frons with an elongated yellow patch; from this patch to the clypeus a very distinct depression, with a rounded elevation in its middle arising from a small, raised fontanelle; mandibles stout, incurved, in lateral view rather strongly curved upwards, 2.3 mm long from the outer base to the apex; left mandible perhaps slightly stouter, with a notch at the base; labrum oval, its base upturned on each side, thinly pilose, with a white triangular soft prolongation at the apex; antennae 17-segmented, reddish brown, paler above and beneath, basal segment thickest, second shorter than the adjacent segments, third about equal to or slightly longer than the following segments, segments from the third onwards gradually becoming somewhat globose; pronotum approximately oval, sides rounded, constricted and concave, middle extending forwards and more strongly backwards, with a fine longitudinal line in the middle; middle with a large, roughly T-shaped pale patch; mesonotum rounded-rectangular, sides upturned, posterior margin slightly concave, with a white patch anteriorly; metanotum about the same in shape but much shorter and broader; legs almost entirely smooth, dark reddish brown, the whole underside together with the legs white with a distinct brownish yellow shade; legs with very few and very fine hairs, especially the tibiae; apical tarsal segment twice as long as the remaining segments together; tibia with two spines beneath, slightly longer than the femur; hind tibia about 11 mm long from the base. Total length 15 mm, head width 5 mm, mandibles 2.3 mm, thorax 4 mm, abdomen 4.5 mm, hind tibia 4 mm, antennae 5 mm. Minor soldier: general shape very similar to T. lilljeborgi, head also black but slightly paler and brownish below, the whole head sometimes dark brown; antennae 17-segmented, second segment much shorter than the adjacent segments; the anterior margin of the pronotum, which is very distinctly emarginate in the middle in T. lilljeborgi, is here only very slightly concave and sometimes almost imperceptible; two of the present specimens are larger, approaching the size of the minor soldier of T. lilljeborgi, the others much smaller. Total length smaller than in T. lilljeborgi (11–12 mm).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Major worker: very similar to that of T. lilljeborgi, third antennal segment much longer than the second; but distinctly smaller, antennal annulations pale brown instead of dark brown, legs white; another good character is that the anterior margin of the pronotum is only very slightly concave in the middle, sometimes almost imperceptible, whereas in T. lilljeborgi it is deeply and very distinctly emarginate. Total length 9 mm, smaller than in T. lilljeborgi (10–12 mm). One specimen still carries a small fragment of cut dry leaf in its mouth.
